source: Minchat Shai on Gen 38:3 (the Masorah; the Toledo-corrected books; Ramban)
claim_en: The Masorah's naming rule: every 'she conceived and bore' takes VA-TIQRA — SHE named — except THREE where HE named (va-yiqra): ER here, Gershom (Exod 2:22), Beriah (Chronicles, outside the instrument). The stream splits exactly: the father names the firstborn (38:3, Ramban: Judah himself), the mother names Onan and Shelah (38:4-5, asserted). A book-variance (some copies read va-tiqra here too) is filed named; the Toledo-corrected books and Onkelos hold the he-form.

le-ER bekhoro ('for Er his FIRSTBORN'): 'this alone is full with vav; every other bekhoro in the Torah is lean' — exact: the one full firstborn-word sits on the son who dies first; the lean pair (Sidon, Uz) asserted.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 38:25 (Bereshit Rabbah 85; R. Huna)
claim_en: hiv mutzet ('SHE was brought out') — written הוא, read as she: R. Huna reads the doubled skeleton — 'SHE and HE were due to come out': when they sentenced her to burning they sentenced the man too, and the written he-form keeps him inside her verse. The written-vav-read-yod mark is in-stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 38:25 (Ketubot 67b, Sotah 10b, Bava Metzia 59a; R. Chananel; the Arukh; the Ritva)
claim_en: mutzet ('brought out') — the furnace-teaching hangs here: better to fall into a fiery furnace than shame a fellow in public, learned from Tamar. R. Chananel's text read the word LEAN of its aleph (mutzat, 'set alight'); the Ritva: 'no book has it so' — and SNAPSHOT writes the aleph: the stream with the books, the kindling-reading surviving as the homily's read-it-as (the Arukh; Rashi on the midrash).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 38:25 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi codices; the Ramah)
claim_en: ve-ha-petilim ('and the CORDS'): the Hilleli codex wrote it lean; the Yerushalmi codex, all the books, and the Ramah rule FULL-OF-FULL — both yods. SNAPSHOT carries both yods: the stream against the Hilleli again, at the very word the recognition turns on.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 38:18 (the Masorah)
claim_en: u-matkha ('and your STAFF') — the Masorah pair, both Torah-side and EXACT: the staff Judah leaves in Tamar's hand, and 'your staff, with which you struck the Nile' (Exod 17:5): the pledge-staff and the miracle-staff share the word's only two stations — the Kitzur: the staff given into her hand is the staff of the wonders.

The Name in the verdict: yehuda hotziuha ve-tisaref + hi (the next verse's first word) — four initials spelling the four-letter Name: 'the Holy One summoned her the signs that had been lost.' The three in-verse initials checked; the fourth (38:25's opening she-word) asserted.

haker na le-mi ha-chotemet ('recognize, please, whose is the seal') — the four words' FINAL letters, read from the last word back, spell tira ('FEAR'): she said to him, fear the One and confess. Ordered finals checked (forward: resh-aleph-yod-tav).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 38:14 (the Masorah)
claim_en: ki gadal ('for Shelah WAS GROWN') — the adjacency stands exactly TWICE in the Torah: Tamar's seeing here, and Isaac's 'until he was grown very GREAT' (26:13): the Kitzur reads the pair toward the kingdom — because she saw 'he was grown,' from her came the royal house that grows until it is very great.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 38:20 (the Masorah)
claim_en: metzaah ('he found her NOT') — the Kitzur's pair: 'because IN THE FIELD he found her' (Deut 22:27, the betrothed maiden) — she was found at the road once and never again. The skeleton's four Torah stations locked: the dove that found no rest (8:9), the road (38:20), the redeemer's sufficiency (Lev 25:28), the field (Deut 22:27).

The chapter's dagesh set, part 1: adulami ('the Adullamite') with the lamed DAGESHED at both stations (38:1 checked, 38:12 asserted); and lo anokhi ('to WHOM I am with child') with the lamed dagesheed at the pledge-speech (asserted) — three hardening dots MS singles out, all in-stream.

The chapter's pointing set, part 2: tiqach ('let her KEEP it') — qof dagesheed, and where MS records the books DIVIDED on the meteg (some on the tav, some on the qof), SNAPSHOT writes BOTH metegs — a both-camps station again (the water-troughs/divide-word class). Also: ha-gedi and gam dagesheed (asserted); hotziuha with tifcha on the aleph (asserted); natan's tav soft with qamatz alone and bet-avikh's bet soft (asserted). DISCREPANCY: titen LI ('what will you give ME') — MS rules the lamed SOFT; SNAPSHOT writes the crowding dagesh (asserted at build): the stream against MS's camp, filed to the watchlist.
